body:
Present on main, independent of #1411.

On an OAuth error or user cancellation the browser never reaches `GET /login`,
so nothing renders the flashed error and the user is sent straight back to the
IdP:

1. blueprints are built with `redirect_to="oauth.<provider>_login"`
   (cps/oauth_bb.py:852, :868, :888)
2. the `oauth_error` handlers only flash() and log.error() — none return a
   response (cps/oauth_bb.py:1029-1080), so flask_dance falls through to
   next_url
3. next_url is `/oauth/link/<provider>`, which does
   `if not <provider>.authorized: return redirect(url_for('<provider>.login'))`
   (cps/oauth_bb.py:1095 github, :1191 generic)
4. `/login/<provider>` starts another IdP trip

Observable symptom: clicking Cancel/Deny at the provider appears to do nothing —
the user bounces back to the provider, and the flashed explanation is never
shown because no login template renders.

`_login_redirect_count` does not detect it: that counter only increments inside
`render_login()` (cps/web.py:2615), which this chain never calls.

Confirmed by source trace during the #1411 review. Not exercised against a live
IdP. #1411 would make this much easier to hit, since it turns every visit to
/login into an automatic provider start.

Likely fix: have the three oauth_error handlers return a redirect to web.login
so the failure lands somewhere that can render the error.
title: Cancelled or failed OAuth loops back to the provider instead of the login page
